body.heading: Collect your leaves
paragraphs: Walk with your adult and pick up leaves that have already fallen. Look for different shapes and colours.
Let muddy leaves dry a little while you have a snack.

body.heading: Glue your picture
paragraphs: Arrange the leaves on paper before you glue. A round leaf might be a sun; a long leaf might be a fish.
Glue them down gently, one at a time. Leaves are fragile, like tiny pieces of the tree's year.

takeaway: A leaf can be a hedgehog's spikes, a tree, or a whole autumn forest.
safetyNotes: Only use leaves that have already fallen; never taste leaves or berries, and wash hands afterwards.
screenFreeExtension: Press a favourite leaf inside a heavy book and use it in a picture next week.
